messages:
alex.k: Quick heads-up — ran into a weird edge case today where the client does a retry after a TCP-level reset and ends up with two partial chunks delivered by the upstream. The gateway treats the reset as final but the downstream resumes and we observe duplicate partial tokens on the client. Repro below.

alex.k: Repro steps: 1) start streaming gen with client deadline 6s; 2) artificially kill upstream conn at 3s (RST); 3) client retries and reattaches; 4) gateway resumes and upstream sends continuation starting from same token window => client sees overlapping tokens.

alex.k: Logs snippet:```
edge: stream resume id=abc123 step=resume upstream=10.0.2.5:443
upstream: reconnect ok, kv-cache window=start:1024
client: recv chunk seq=12 tokens="...the quick"
client: recv chunk seq=13 tokens=" quick brown"
```

maria: ugh. i've seen similar when resume token bookkeeping isn't atomically advanced before signaling completion. are we sure the resume token is persisted before we ack the client EOF? :thinking:

alex.k: that's my suspicion — race between marking lease ended and checkpointing the resume token to the session header. If the RST races with the persist, we fall back to optimistic resume and replay overlap.

sahil: two obvious paths: 1) make resume checkpoint durable before any final ack to client (adds latency on the slow path), or 2) emit an idempotency envelope so client can dedupe overlapping tokens.

jen: +1 to sahil's options. Also consider weak read-after-write: persist token to in-memory session then replicate async, but include a session-epoch in the resume handshake so newer resumes that don't see the epoch refuse to replay. That keeps common case fast.

alex.k: sketch of handshake tweak: on resume request include resume_epoch and last_persisted_seq. Edge verifies epoch==current_session_epoch OR fails fast (client must do full reconnect). Pseudocode:```
resume_request { session_id, resume_epoch, last_seq }
if resume_epoch != session.epoch || last_seq < session.persisted_seq { return REJECT; }
apply_resume();
```

maria: sounds good. question: where do we store epoch? in session metadata (redis/etcd) or in local lease state? If global store -> slower but consistent across frontends; local -> risk of split-brain on failover.

sahil: keep authoritative epoch in the control plane (kv-store), but cache lease epoch locally for fast path reads. Writes that advance epoch need to be two-phase (local update + control-plane persist). If local update fails to persist — we must reject resume from other nodes which is ok.

jen: what about gating by connection-origin? If downstream already saw tokens, we should allow idempotent writes for same connection id. But that doesn't help new client retrying from other IPs.

alex.k: implementation concerns: 1) we must avoid adding path-sensitive latency on every chunk; epoch checks only on resume handshake. 2) persist-on-finalize only — for long stream we checkpoint periodic snapshot (every N tokens) to keep last_seq bounded.

maria: operationally, this means adding a small reconciliation job to garbage collect orphaned sessions where epoch != control-plane and no active lease for X minutes. Also add metric: resume_rejects / resume_successes.

sahil: also include client-side guidance: add idempotency token to resume attempts and have SDK dedupe partial tokens by seq window. doc blurb can help reduce risk while we roll the server change.

alex.k: plan proposal: A) short-term: SDK docs + client idempotency token; B) mid-term: implement resume_epoch + last_seq handshake + control-plane persist for epoch; C) long-term: explore KV-cache checkpointing optimization so per-chunk persists aren't needed. Thoughts?

jen: +1. timeline: B is ~2 sprints (backend + e2e tests + migration), A is immediate. I can take spearhead on tests.

maria: i'll draft ops playbook for session orphan detection and metrics.

deploy-bot: Reminder: canary deployment for edge-proxy v2 scheduled 03/28 02:00 UTC — will include healthcheck changes only.

alex.k: thanks all. I'll open RFC PR with the handshake sketch and add test vectors for overlapping token streams. If anyone wants to pair on the test harness ping me. :thumbsup:
